out_items.name: Person in charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties

violations.title: Permit to Operate Posted in Conspicuous Location
violations.corrective_action: A valid permit shall be posted in every food establishment in a conspicuous place in the public view. Food establishment permits are issued for a calendar year and expire on December 31 regardless of the month of issue. POST 2026 FOOD ESTABLISHMENT PERMIT. CONTACT [county email] FOR A COPY IF NEEDED.

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food
violations.observation: A review of the menu with the foodservice operator indicates that there is no consumer advisory for the following food item(s) that may be served raw and/or undercooked: TUNA TARTARE ON JUNE SPECIALS MENU.
violations.corrective_action: If an animal food such as beef, eggs, fish, lamb, milk, pork, poultry, or shellfish is served or sold raw or undercooked the permit holder shall inform consumers of the significantly increased risk of consuming such foods by way of a disclosure and reminder using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means. CFM WILL ADD DISCLOSURE AND REMINDER VIA TABLE CARD OR LABEL TO MENU.

violations.title: Cooking Raw Animal Foods, Minimum of 165F
violations.observation: The following poultry item was not cooked to a sufficient temperature and/or time to eliminate pathogenic bacteria: chicken breast (119F) from grill.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods such as poultry, wild game animals, stuffed fish, stuffed meat, stuffed pasta, stuffed poultry, stuffed ratites, or stuffing containing any of these raw animal foods shall be cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 165F for at least 15 seconds. PIC cooked all chicken to an internal temperature of 165F.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours: cooked chicken and andouille gumbo (60-68F, after >6 hours) in 2 door upright display at dish pit.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. PIC discarded gumbo. The Main Street Pub (Inspection Date: 10/15/2025) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: cut tomato (46F) in 2 door upright at front; pico de gallo (44F) in 2 door upright display at dish pit.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC discarded tomato and pico de gallo.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Storage-Personal Care Items
violations.observation: Observed personal keys, lotions, and ointments stored in such a way that they could contaminate prep surface of 2 door flattop unit at dish pit.
violations.corrective_action: All employees' personal care items shall be stored in a way that prevents the contamination of food and food contact surfaces through improper labeling or storage. PIC placed all personal items in designated storage.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: observed large volumes of chicken and andouille gumbo cooling in covered containers at the bottom of 2 door upright display at dish.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. PIC discarded gumbo and educated staff on proper procedure for the cooling of large portions of gumbo and similar menu items.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: Observed salmon fillets stored in sealed reduced oxygen packaging to thaw in 2 door flattop at dish pit.
violations.corrective_action: PIC removed packaging for the continuation of the thawing process.

violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program
violations.observation: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager who has shown proficiency through passing an accredited examination. Observed no CFM present at beginning of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Obtain a certified food managers certificate from an accredited program. CFM arrived during inspection. The Main Street Pub (Inspection Date: 04/23/2025) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw shell eggs on shelf above RTE deli meats in Deli Display case.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CFM removed raw shell eggs from unit.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: Observed previously frozen salmon thawing in intact packaging.
violations.corrective_action: Follow thawing instructions on frozen salmon stating to remove from packaging before thawing.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: oil, clarified butter, water in squeeze bottles at cookline.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. CFM will label secondary containers with food name.

violations.title: Hair Restraints
violations.observation: Employees observed working in the food service area without proper hair restraints. Observed 2 female and 1 male employee working in food preparation without wearing hair net/hat/visor.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. CFM discussed with employees that proper hair restraints must be worn during food preparation.
